about: OH campaign art (Lane A1, 2026-10-02): the source for scripts/generate-oh-art.mjs. Every hero slide, deal tile (with its tall bento variant), room tile and room banner is a generated scene (no product, no text, no marks) with the piece's lead product placed on it from LG's own cutout in public/oh/img/products/, so nothing on the art is a model's guess at a product. Headline, sub, badge and button are content the page draws over the art. A verdict in gate holds only for the sha256 of the exact WebP reviewed; a changed byte reads pending. Tones (lane A1b, 2026-10-03): the base keys below are A1's night set (tone dark); tones.light is A1b's daylight recipe over them (style, aspect framing, scenes, scrims, shadows, scene filter, encoders, and each job's pick, position, lift, scrim and verdict; never a product's size). defaultTone names the tone the generator composes when --tone is not given.
style: Photographic campaign image for a premium home-electronics and home-appliance store's homepage, in the family of a flagship electronics brand's own website banners: rich, dark, cinematic and uncluttered, with one soft colour glow. Straight-on, eye-level camera with a level horizon and one-point perspective; sharp focus; photographic realism; soft, believable light. ABSOLUTELY NO text, NO letters, NO numbers, NO logos, NO brand marks, NO signage, NO posters or artwork with writing, NO watermarks, NO people, NO hands, NO faces, NO pets. NO television, NO screen, NO monitor, NO speaker and NO appliance anywhere in the frame.

wide.frame: Wide banner framing: the left three fifths are calm, dark and simple (a plain, softly lit wall with no objects of interest), ready for a white headline; the right two fifths hold {area}, empty and softly lit.

card.frame: Card framing: the right half holds {area}, empty and softly lit; the left half is calm, dark and simple, ready for a white headline; the bottom edge falls off to shadow.

tall.frame: Portrait card framing: {area} fills the upper middle of the frame, empty and softly lit; below it the same floor continues seamlessly to the bottom edge, fading gradually into deep shadow, with no band, no step and no edge across it, calm and plain, ready for a white headline.

banner-tall.note: The room banner for a taller banner box (M1e, about 490 px at 1440): the banner's own scene extended upward from the same bottom edge, the product at the very pixel size and scene position it has in the 1440x360 banner (its box is computed on the banner's frame, never this one).

largeSource.note: Where D2 has an accepted 840 cutout (MANIFEST.json large), hero slides, room banners and any tile or tall tile that would scale the 420 cutout above 1.0x draw the 840 file instead, into the same box the 420 fit gives, so every zone holds. Pixel treatments are stated at the 420 scale and scaled with the file.
